ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a family of common-emitter transistor output characteristic curves, with the vertical axis labeled i_C/mA and the horizontal axis labeled u_CE/V, and an I_B=0 label at the bottom. Multiple approximately horizontal output characteristic curves are arranged from bottom to top, and a fixed DC load line slopes from upper left to lower right. The two quiescent operating points Q1 and Q2 are both on the same load line, where Q2 is located to the upper left of Q1, that is, it corresponds to a larger collector current and lies on a higher output characteristic curve. Reasoning: The load line of the fixed-bias common-emitter amplifier circuit has not changed, and the operating point moving from Q1 to Q2 means that under the same load-line condition the quiescent collector current increases. Interpreting the family of curves in the figure, a higher output characteristic curve means that a larger collector current can be obtained under the same base excitation; and the transistor current amplification factor beta characterizes the amplification ability from base current to collector current. Therefore, the upward movement from Q1 to Q2 indicates that the transistor current amplification factor increases.
